creator: behindthesale
text: I think the cheaper the item to purchase, the more respective margin I want from it. So if I buy an item for £50 and can get £100 for it, that’s a very nice x2 margin bringing in £50 profit in one sale (before fees etc). But if I buy something for £1, it’s absolutely not worth my time and effort to aim for a x2 margin to make £2. Really the very lowest I’d want for a £1 is probably £5, and that’s still only a £4 profit regardless of margins. I try to imagine it like making a salary. Is it worth my time to source, clean, steam, list and post an item for a £1 profit? To me it’s not, it’s not close to even minimum wage. Clearly it’s more of a Wholesaler business model as they can do it thousands of times over quickly, but for the average reseller at home doing it all themselves it’s not realistic imo. I also think hand picking is better than buying blind bales so you can have full control over what you sell. But to level up and increase your revenue to a true business level, you would have to get bales etc in as you couldn’t handpick everything at that scale.
